column1: # Finance functions. One row per function, per task it belongs to. Tab-separated; see finder.py for the rules.

column7: summary
Holds an exact amount with four decimal places, for money that needs no more.
Holds an exact decimal number with up to 28 places, for rates, prices and results.
Parses text into a Decimal exactly; returns empty on bad input or over 28 places.
Parses text into a Currency exactly; returns empty on bad input or over four places.
Returns a Currency of a whole number of units, exactly.
Returns a Currency from whole units and a ten-thousandths part, exactly.
Returns a Currency from its stored integer, which is the amount times 10000.
Converts a double to a Currency, rounded to four decimal places.
Returns a 64-bit integer as a Decimal, exactly.
Returns an unsigned 64-bit integer as a Decimal, exactly.
Returns a whole number over a power of ten as a Decimal: 1999 at scale 2 is 19.99.
Builds a Decimal from three 32-bit mantissa words, a sign flag and a scale.
Converts a double to a Decimal of 15 significant digits; NaN or infinity gives Invalid.
Converts a Currency to a Decimal, exactly.
Returns false if the Currency is Invalid; the only reliable test for a bad value.
Returns the stored integer, the amount times 10000, for saving to a file or database.
Returns the amount as a double, which loses precision above about 900 billion.
Returns -1, 0 or 1 comparing two Decimals by value, or -2 if either is Invalid.
Returns zero, the same value a new Decimal starts with.
Returns one as a Decimal.
Returns minus one as a Decimal.
Returns the most negative value a Decimal can hold.
Returns the largest value a Decimal can hold.
Returns the Invalid Decimal, which overflow and division by zero also produce.
Returns the Invalid Currency, which overflow also produces; it never equals anything.
Returns the amount rounded up to a whole unit, towards positive infinity.
Returns the amount rounded to 0 to 4 places by a rounding rule you name.
Splits a Currency total by weights into parts that add up to it exactly.
Splits a Decimal total by weights, at a scale you choose, into parts that add up exactly.
Adds an amount times a rate to a running total, rounding only once at the end.
Adds an amount times a fraction, such as one third, to a running total exactly.
Returns the running total as a Currency, rounded once; reading it does not reset it.
Holds a rounding policy: decimal places, rounding mode, and whether to round each amount.
Returns a rounding policy with the places, mode and round-each flag you choose.
Returns the default policy: two places, half-to-even, every posted amount rounded.
Returns a policy of four places, half-to-even, to match a Currency ledger.
Returns a policy that never rounds, to keep full precision or see what rounding costs.
Rounds a Decimal by a policy, or returns it unchanged if the policy does not round.
Holds why a finance call failed: a code, a message and, for solvers, how close it got.
Lists the failure codes, such as FIN_INVALID_RATE and FIN_NO_SIGN_CHANGE.
Returns a short, fixed English description of a failure code.
Lists how often interest compounds, as periods per year, plus simple and continuous.
Returns a quoted annual rate divided by its compounding periods, exactly.
Returns what a quoted annual rate really earns in a year once it compounds.
Returns the quoted annual rate that earns a given effective yearly return.
Restates a quoted annual rate for a different compounding frequency.
Returns the continuously compounded rate that gives an effective yearly return.
Returns the effective yearly return of a continuously compounded rate.
Returns the rate per payment when compounding and payment frequency differ.
Returns principal times rate times a fraction of a year, exactly.
Returns simple interest between two dates on a day-count basis you choose.
Lists the six day-count bases, such as actual/365 fixed and 30/360 US.
Counts the days between two dates on a day-count basis.
Returns the fraction of a year between two dates on a basis, as an exact Decimal.
Returns the fraction of a year between two dates on a basis, as a double.
Returns what one unit grows to over a whole number of periods at a rate, exactly.
Returns what one unit due after a whole number of periods is worth today.
Returns what one unit grows to over a fractional number of periods.
Returns what one unit grows to over a number of years with continuous compounding.
Holds rate, periods, payment, present value, future value and timing for annuity sums.
Returns annuity terms from the six values; the one being solved for is ignored.
Lists whether payments fall at the end or at the start of each period.
Returns what a stream of payments plus a final amount is worth today.
Returns what a stream of payments will be worth at the end of the term.
Returns the level payment per period, negative when the present value is positive.
Returns a single future amount discounted back a number of periods.
Returns a single amount compounded forward a number of periods.
Returns how many periods a payment takes to clear a balance, as a fractional double.
Returns how many payments clear a balance, rounded up to a whole number.
Returns the rate per period implied by a known payment, value and term.
Returns what one unit paid each period is worth today.
Returns what one unit paid each period grows to by the end of the term.
Holds a loan's principal, rate, term, frequencies, rounding and first payment date.
Returns loan terms with the payment frequency and compounding you choose.
Returns loan terms for a US mortgage: monthly compounding and monthly payments.
Returns loan terms for a Canadian mortgage: semi-annual compounding, monthly payments.
Lists how often payments are made, including weekly and accelerated biweekly.
Returns a loan's level payment, rounded once; the last payment absorbs the remainder.
Returns the annual rate implied by a known principal, payment and term.
Returns the annual rate once financed fees are counted as a cost of borrowing.
Returns a loan's amortization schedule, built lazily, to walk with for each.
Holds a loan schedule's terms and gives its scheduled payment count and payment.
Walks a loan schedule row by row, for stopping early or reading a window.
Holds one period: due date, balances, payment, interest, principal and running totals.
Returns every row of a loan schedule as an Array, for random access.
Returns one row of a loan schedule, rounded exactly as it would be posted.
Returns the balance after a period from a formula, without walking the schedule.
Returns the interest posted across a range of periods, such as one tax year.
Returns the principal repaid across a range of periods, extra payments included.
Returns what settles a loan on a date: the balance plus interest accrued since.
Returns a loan's totals, payment count and payoff date, and what extra payments save.
Holds what LoanSummarize returns: payments, totals, effective rate and savings.
Holds extra principal paid over a range of periods; overlapping ranges add up.
Returns a single extra principal payment made in one period.
Returns the same extra principal payment in every period of a range.
Holds an amount and the date it happens, for the dated value and return functions.
Returns a cash flow on a date; the dates in a series must ascend.
Returns a cash flow with no date, placed by its period number.
Returns the net present value of flows at a rate; the first flow is not discounted.
Returns the net present value carried forward to the end of the series.
Returns the net present value of dated flows at an annual rate on a day-count basis.
Returns the rate at which the net present value of a series of flows is zero.
Returns the internal rate of return of flows on irregular dates.
Returns a rate of return with one answer, from separate finance and reinvestment rates.
Returns when the running total of flows turns positive, or empty if it never does.
Returns when the running total of discounted flows turns positive, or empty if never.
Returns the present value of the later flows divided by the initial outlay.
Holds an asset's cost, salvage value, life in periods and declining-balance factor.
Returns depreciation terms from cost, salvage and life, with a factor of 2 and cents.
Lists the six methods, from straight line to units of production.
Returns one period's expense, with cost less salvage spread evenly over the life.
Returns one period's expense as a fixed fraction of the remaining book value.
Returns one period's expense at twice the straight-line rate, never below salvage.
Returns one period's expense, weighted by how many periods of the life are left.
Returns one period's expense from the units it produced out of the lifetime total.
Returns the full schedule for a method, including declining balance with a switch.
Holds every period of a write-off, to walk with for each.
Walks a depreciation schedule row by row, for stopping early.
Holds one period: opening and closing book value, expense and depreciation so far.
Returns every row of a depreciation schedule as an Array.
Lists how many observations make a year: annual, quarterly, monthly, weekly or daily.
Returns the gain plus income over a holding period, as a fraction of the start value.
Returns the steady yearly rate that grows a starting value to an ending value.
Converts a return per period to a yearly return by compounding, not multiplying.
Converts a total return over a number of observations to a yearly return.
Returns sub-period returns linked by compounding, ignoring when money moved in or out.
Returns an approximate time-weighted return, weighting each flow by days invested.
Returns the dated internal rate of return of contributions and the closing value.
Returns the compounded return after each observation, as a growth chart plots.
Returns the sample standard deviation of returns, annualized.
Returns the annualized shortfall of returns below a target, ignoring gains.
Returns the worst fall from a peak to a later low, as a positive fraction.
Returns the index of the peak the worst drawdown fell from, or empty if none.
Returns the index of the low point of the worst drawdown, or empty if none.
Returns the fall from the running peak at each observation, zero or negative.
Returns the annualized return above the risk-free rate per unit of volatility.
Returns the annualized return above a target per unit of downside deviation.
Returns total and yearly return, volatility, Sharpe, Sortino and drawdown in one call.
Holds the figures SummarizeReturns computes, one field each.
Returns how much an asset moves when its benchmark moves by one.
Returns the annualized return beyond what the asset's beta to its benchmark explains.
Returns the annualized standard deviation of the asset's return less the benchmark's.
Returns the return above the benchmark per unit of tracking error.
Returns how closely an asset moves with its benchmark, from -1 to 1.
Finds where your function is zero between two bounds, and reports how close it got.
Holds a pointer to the function the root finder calls with a value and a context.
Holds the root finder's bounds, starting guess, tolerances and iteration limits.
Returns the standard solver settings: rate bounds, 128 iterations and no guess.
Returns the standard solver settings with a starting guess.
Holds the root found, its residual, the iteration count and whether it converged.
